summary: Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. She held positions at Jadavpur, Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, Utrecht University (senior lecturer, 1968–1986), and Oxford (teacher, 1990–2000).

Sanne Dokter-Mersch is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at Leiden University (around 2016–2021) under doctoral supervisors Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi, with Jonathan A. Silk, Hans T. Bakker, and Elizabeth Ann Cecil on her committee.

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw and at Harvard University. He taught at the University of Yangon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised Myanmar's Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Sara Boin-Webb was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jean Dantinne. From around 1983 to 2005, she served as an editor for Buddhist Studies Review.

Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD), supervised by Tom J. F. Tillemans. She was professor at Wisconsin-Madison (2002–2005) and became associate professor at Emory in 2005.

Sara Marie Conrad is a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her MA at Indiana University by 2012, where her committee members included Gendun Rabsal, Elliot Sperling, and Joëlle Bahloul.

Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (2008–2016) supervised by Jenny Purtle, having also studied under numerous teachers including Khenpo Kunga Sherab and John C. Huntington.

Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Michigan and Kobe. Her academic posts include associate professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).
Sarah Harding is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpön Lama Tenpa. She held a post at Naropa University in 2008.

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University (around 1991–2001) under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College from around 2001 to 2005.

Sarah Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and the University of Virginia, and later held academic posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (appointed 2009).

Sarah Shaw is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She holds membership in Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies and Wolfson College, and is an honorary fellow at the OCBS.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He worked at the University of Calcutta from around 1939 to 1976 and served as librarian at the Asiatic Society in 1943.

Sarat Chandra Das was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied civil engineering at Presidency University, Kolkata, and received instruction from Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel.
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Manipur University under the supervision of S. Shyamkishore Singh, having also studied under S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Saroja Bhate is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from around 1972 to 2002 and as honorary secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 2002 to 2005.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religion educated at Madras Christian College. His appointments included professorships at Calcutta and Oxford, vice chancellorship of Banaras Hindu University, chancellorship of the University of Delhi, and presidency of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.
Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta.

Satiranjan Sen was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University. He served as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

Satischandra Vidyabhusana was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He studied under Sarat Chandra Das, earned a PhD from Calcutta University, taught at Presidency University, served as principal of Sanskrit College, and was joint philological secretary at the Asiatic Society.
